Matched RecHarness Amazon task: four datasets Movies_and_TV,
Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics, CDs_and_Vinyl, macro-average validation
HR@10. Start from RecHarness sasrec_perdataset. Preprocessing seed=0 and training
seed=42, exactly as run2.sh. The host executes your train.py and then independently
evaluates working/predict.py using the pinned RecHarness benchmark (200 validation
users/category, 99 unique negative candidates, evaluation seed=42). Test labels and
test metrics are unavailable during search. Retain all four categories and dataset
routing. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath
your trial directory, as the baseline does. Training may change model architecture,
loss, optimizer, sampling and hyperparameters, as in RecHarness. Do not alter input
splits, invent metrics, read hidden test files, fetch extra datasets/pretrained weights,
or change the host evaluator. Changes to inference must also update the predictor
writer so working/predict.py loads the trained architecture. Keep execution single-GPU;
the host provides four concurrent trial slots and 64 CPU cores. No shell actions,
filesystem inspection, or training tools are needed in the LLM call: return code.
All training, diagnostics, debugging and failed trials consume the method's shared
43,200 GPU-second search budget. LLM time and final held-out inference are recorded
separately, matching run2.sh's separate final-evaluation step.
The original RecHarness tools layer sets SASREC_EPOCHS=200 (overriding the template's
standalone default of 300); this same environment default applies here.

METHOD: self_evolverec

Diagnostic task adapter: diagnosis_tools.py must retain class DiagnosisProbe(view, device)
and method run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions.
It must also retain callable diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), returning
the diagnostic interpretation prompt using measured metrics and their definitions.
view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis uses item embeddings (`item_emb.weight`), sequence features from `log2feats(sequence)`, and candidate logits from `predict_score(features, items)`. Model internals are not supplied, so the sequence encoder and final user representation cannot be identified. The margin probe evaluates all valid sequence positions rather than explicitly selecting a final-position representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` stores the compatibility view and its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Only metadata is subsequently consulted; reviews and histories are not directly analyzed.

The loader yields `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with tensors shaped B × L. Sequences pass through `log2feats`; positive and negative IDs are stacked into B × L × 2 candidates for `predict_score`. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded. Margin evaluation uses evaluation mode and disables gradients.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`:** Samples at most 2,048 non-padding item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result through `(cosine + 1) / 2`. Higher values indicate directional alignment; approximately 0.5 indicates average cosine near zero. This alone does not establish recommendation diversity.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`:** Mean and lower tenth percentile of positive minus negative logits across up to ten training batches. Larger values indicate stronger sampled separation.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`:** Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`:** Fraction below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs, although the threshold depends on logit scale.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`:** Counts categories of positive and negative items in low-margin and wrong-ranking cases, retaining the top twenty categories per group. Item categories are unavailable in this task, so these lists provide no supported category diagnosis.

# Perturbation & Tests

There are no sequence perturbations, shuffling tests, or sensitivity comparisons. Random embedding sampling and loader-provided negatives are the only sampling mechanisms.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into a prompt requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; it does not itself generate that interpretation.

These probes do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, temporal sensitivity, gradients, or simulator traits. Training-sample margins depend on negative sampling; missing valid positions produce zero-valued margin summaries rather than an explicit missing-data signal.

Recent work supports separating evidence relations from recommendation relevance. [CLUE (2025 preprint; ACL 2026)](https://aclanthology.org/2026.acl-long.2110/) grounds uncertainty explanations in specific agreeing or conflicting text spans. Applied here: extract atomic claims from titles/descriptions, attach supporting passages, and distinguish supported matches, explicit contradictions, and insufficient evidence. A stated device requirement plus missing ownership evidence means “prerequisite unverified”; it does not establish incompatibility. Shared topic words support content similarity, not connector, edition, region, or platform compatibility. These are proposed adaptations, not validated recommendation findings.

Repeat-purchase research emphasizes timing rather than blanket duplicate penalties. [MgRIA (2026)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S1567422326000037) models multiple repurchase cycles; the earlier [Scalable Demand-Aware Recommendation](https://arxiv.org/abs/1702.06347) explicitly distinguishes durable from nondurable demand through interpurchase duration. For this task, flag recent, textually similar durable-item recommendations as possible redundancy, with evidence and elapsed time. Histories alone cannot establish continued ownership, fulfilled need, or dislike; unseen-item filtering also does not eliminate near-duplicate products.

[Abstention evaluation (COLING 2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.627/) treats withholding unsupported answers as a distinct reliability capability. [Selection-conditional conformal inference (2025)](https://academic.oup.com/jrsssb/article/87/4/1239/8113856) highlights that selection affects coverage guarantees. Practical implication: calibrate diagnostic assertions against available qualitative feedback, reporting assertion coverage, error among asserted cases, and category-specific confusion between contradiction and unknown. Twenty users provide exploratory evidence, not strong calibration guarantees. Abstain from unsupported diagnostic claims while preserving ranked recommendations and the fixed macro HR@10 selection objective; uncertainty must not become a negative-preference label.

view.model is the actual trained nn.Module. view.item_emb, log2feats(sequence),
predict_score(features, items), user_train, meta_data, review_data implement the
initial SASRec compatibility contract. Adapt probes when changing the architecture.
train_loader yields (None, sequence, positive, negative), tensors of shape B x L.
Only public interaction histories, item titles, descriptions and timestamps are available.
Review ratings/text, item ratings/categories/prices/stores are NOT available in this
shared RecHarness task. Never invent them. Simulator diversity/conformity traits are
explicitly unobserved. Twenty real training users (five/category) receive full-catalog
unseen-item recommendations, as the native simulator requires. Selection uses the
common macro validation HR@10, replacing the native HR@5/NDCG@5 combined score.

## Current Code Workflow (from code analyzer)
# Model Overview (for Diagnosis)

Diagnosis uses item embeddings (`item_emb.weight`), sequence features from `log2feats(sequence)`, and candidate logits from `predict_score(features, items)`. Model internals are not supplied, so the sequence encoder and final user representation cannot be identified. The margin probe evaluates all valid sequence positions rather than explicitly selecting a final-position representation.

# Diagnosis Inputs & Hooks

`DiagnosisProbe(model, device)` stores the compatibility view and its `meta_data`, `review_data`, and `user_train`. Only metadata is subsequently consulted; reviews and histories are not directly analyzed.

The loader yields `(None, sequence, positive, negative)` with tensors shaped B × L. Sequences pass through `log2feats`; positive and negative IDs are stacked into B × L × 2 candidates for `predict_score`. Positions with positive ID zero are excluded. Margin evaluation uses evaluation mode and disables gradients.

# Probes & Metrics

- **`embedding_collapse_score`:** Samples at most 2,048 non-padding item embeddings using seed 42, normalizes them, averages off-diagonal cosine similarities, and maps the result through `(cosine + 1) / 2`. Higher values indicate directional alignment; approximately 0.5 indicates average cosine near zero. This alone does not establish recommendation diversity.
- **`pos_neg_margin_mean` / `pos_neg_margin_p10`:** Mean and lower tenth percentile of positive minus negative logits across up to ten training batches. Larger values indicate stronger sampled separation.
- **`pos_neg_neg_beats_pos_rate`:** Fraction of margins below zero; lower is better.
- **`pos_neg_small_margin_rate`:** Fraction below 0.5; lower indicates fewer weakly separated pairs, although the threshold depends on logit scale.
- **`pos_neg_margin_category_breakdown`:** Counts categories of positive and negative items in low-margin and wrong-ranking cases, retaining the top twenty categories per group. Item categories are unavailable in this task, so these lists provide no supported category diagnosis.

# Perturbation & Tests

There are no sequence perturbations, shuffling tests, or sensitivity comparisons. Random embedding sampling and loader-provided negatives are the only sampling mechanisms.

# MODEL_DIAGNOSIS Schema & Limitations

`run_full_diagnosis` returns `metrics` and `metric_definitions`. `diagnosis_interpreter_prompt` embeds both into a prompt requesting JSON with `status`, `core_findings`, `key_implications`, and `evidence`; it does not itself generate that interpretation.

These probes do not measure validation HR@10, full-catalog ranking, temporal sensitivity, gradients, or simulator traits. Training-sample margins depend on negative sampling; missing valid positions produce zero-valued margin summaries rather than an explicit missing-data signal.
